newsitem.title: USA: Sun sets additional $150 mln shr buyback.
newsitem.headline: Sun sets additional $150 mln shr buyback.

text.p: Sun Co Inc said Thursday its board authorized an additional $150 million to buy back its shares, as it reported a rising operating income for the second quarter.
The company posted operating income of $105 million for the second quarter, or $1.07 a share, compared with $50 million, or $0.50 a share, for the year earlier quarter.
Sun's earnings resoundingly beat a First Call poll of 18 analysts who had put the company's earnings at $0.77 a share for the quarter.

The company also earned $105 million in net income in the second quarter, compared with a loss of $3 million in 1996, or $0.19 loss per share, when Sun took an after-tax charge of $53 million to write down assets.

"The dramatic increase in earnings resulted from improved operating performance across all of Sun's businesses, not from an improvement in overall market conditions," said chief executive Robert Campbell in a statement.

Sun's Northeast Refining reported a $37 million operating income in the quarter, compared with $4 million in 1996. The refiner attributed the rise to $35 million in expense cutting and rising input of 494,000 barrels a day, or 103 percent of rated capacity.
Slightly higher margins for gasoline were offset by the impact five percent lower retail gasoline volumes, Sun said.
Sun's Sunoco Northeast Marketing division earned $17 million in the quarter, compared with $7 million a year ago. The company attributed the rise mostly to cost cutting measures totaling $17 million.

The company's Sunoco Chemicals division doubled its operating income to $22 million in the second quarter from $11 million in 1996 because of higher production levels of 23,200 barrels per day (bpd) from 19,500 bpd and improved profit margins on most products.

Sun's Sunoco MidAmerica Marketing & Refining posted an operating income of $20 million, compared with a $5 million income in the second quarter of last year. The refiner ascribed the improvement to higher production to 138,100 bpd, or 110 percent of capacity, and higher wholesale refining and chemical margins and lower costs.

Sun's lubricants business earned $2 million in the quarter, compared with a $3 million loss in 1996. The company said higher margins for value-added lubricants more than offset the effect of lower base oil margins.
The company's stock closed at 31-1/8 Wednesday, close to its 52-week high of 32-5/8.
